21.title: CPU reference renderer
milestones: P21-A: image contract and byte-checked PPM output.
P21-B: six-plane homogeneous clipping with attributed vertices.
P21-C: quantized coverage, depth and perspective-correct UVs with comparison images.
P21-D: a sphere or triangle ray path and BVH/brute-force comparison.
evidence: Coordinate contract; unit tests; clipped polygon dumps; coverage-count proof.
Affine/corrected images; near-plane sequence; BVH seed and raw build/query measurements.
review: Why should the renderer keep an image byte test even when screenshots look right?
Viewers can reinterpret color and hide flips or padding issues. Exact byte and marker tests verify the actual output contract.
Can a triangle with every original vertex outside the frustum still have visible area?
Yes. It can cross the view volume; correct polygon clipping may create visible intersection vertices.
Which attributes use reciprocal-w interpolation, and what is the depth exception here?
Smooth surface attributes such as UVs use the ratio. Conventional projected z_ndc is already interpolated affinely in screen coordinates.
What does a BVH correctness test compare besides execution time?
Hit/miss, nearest primitive identity and t under a stated tie/tolerance policy, using an independent brute-force oracle.
Why not promise exact GPU image equality for the CPU reference?
Subpixel precision, coverage, sample positions, color formats and floating behavior can differ; compare under declared conventions and tolerances.

22.title: One validated GPU route
milestones: P22-A: capability report, clear target and validation capture.
P22-B: geometry, transform layout and bounded compute readback.
P22-C: compute-to-draw dependency and two reusable contexts.
P22-D: resizing, loss policy and failure-safe teardown.
evidence: Actual backend/toolchain record; byte layout table; shader sources; readback results.
Dependency ledger; frame-context stress log; resize/minimize matrix; pending hardware markers where applicable.
review: Why can correct submission order still be an incomplete native synchronization argument?
The resource may also require memory availability/visibility, a transition or ownership transfer under the API rules.
Are WebGPU implicit transitions proof that Vulkan barriers are unnecessary?
No. The managed API supplies different validation and transition behavior; native dependencies still need native expression.
What separates frame-context indices from presentation-image indices?
They identify different ownership pools and may have different counts and acquisition order.
Why should GPU results include readback instead of only a triangle?
A visual output may not reveal tail bounds or exact compute errors. Numeric readback validates the tested data path.
What can a CPU-only run honestly establish for this module?
The ledger, layout arithmetic and other host models; not driver hazard freedom, actual GPU output or GPU performance.

23.title: Material and lighting laboratory
milestones: P23-A: linear-light diffuse and documented microfacet material.
P23-B: semantic mip filtering and tangent-handedness tests.
P23-C: one shadow map and an equal-quality lighting-path comparison.
P23-D: exposure, tone mapping and temporal failure/rejection sequences.
evidence: Units/space table; raw linear fixtures; material grid; normal seam test.
Buffer budget; light-count data; shadow-bias comparison; temporal sequence and error domain.
review: Why distinguish radiance from irradiance in a shader notebook?
They have different directional/area units and roles in transport; mixing them can hide missing cosine or normalization factors.
Why can a perfect normal-map seam on one mesh be insufficient?
Mirrored UVs, degenerate parameterization and nonuniform scaling expose different tangent-frame failures.
Why is a lower light-list count not a measured speedup?
List construction, lookup, memory and GPU execution overhead also contribute; measure the equal-quality workload.
Does an HDR intermediate prove HDR display output?
No. The engine may tone-map the intermediate to an SDR surface; display negotiation and color handling are separate.
Why preserve camera-cut and disocclusion failures in the report?
They demonstrate the limits and behavior of correspondence/rejection rather than concealing temporal artifacts behind still images.

24.title: Headless engine core
milestones: P24-A: fixed ticks, interpolation and explicit overload accounting.
P24-B: generational identity and deferred structural edits.
P24-C: checked arena plus serial/parallel task-graph validation.
P24-D: schema migration, transactional loads and safe reload/shutdown.
evidence: Tick-indexed input log; time invariant tests; entity mutation tests.
Task trace and critical path; arena guard tests; save fixtures; stale reload and initialization-failure logs.
review: What does dropping accumulated ticks sacrifice?
Simulation no longer tracks all elapsed real time; this must be compatible with the product and recorded explicitly.
Why is a valid handle lookup not permission to hold a component pointer forever?
Subsequent structural changes can move or destroy storage even while logical identity remains meaningful.
Can an acyclic task graph still race?
Yes. Missing edges or undeclared overlapping writes permit unsafe simultaneous access.
What makes a load transactional?
It constructs and validates a full candidate before publication, leaving the old world unchanged if any step fails.
What protects against an old reload overwriting a new one?
Request/revision tokens checked at completion and publication, plus safe retirement of discarded candidates.

25.title: Gate E integrated engine
milestones: P25-A: reproducible mesh/image cooking with dependency-aware keys.
P25-B: bounded loading, cancellation and peak-budget evidence.
P25-C: validated inspector commands and undo/redo histories.
P25-D: clean build, measurements, second-person review and Gate E defense.
evidence: Source/cooked manifest and provenance; cold/warm/change/corruption tests.
Peak residency ledger; ten-command history tests; raw timings; reviewer record; explicit limitations.
review: Which key inputs prevent a stale content build after a tool upgrade?
Tool/importer version, target format, semantic settings, source digest and dependency digests.
Why can bounded worker count still exceed the memory budget?
Each worker or queue stage can retain multiple large decoded/staging allocations; bound bytes and overlap, not just threads.
What must happen to editor history when its target scene revision is replaced?
Clear it or apply a deliberately revision-aware remapping policy; never replay stale commands blindly.
What does the software-only Gate E allowance exclude?
Untested GPU support, hazard-freedom and timing claims. CPU integration, ownership, cooking, inspection and other mandatory evidence still apply.
What must a reviewer reproduce besides opening a screenshot?
A clean build/run, a boundary test, a live edit and save/reload under the README, followed by the learner explaining dependencies and tradeoffs.
